A protection mandate covers property and/or the person and is executed only after incapacity and court homologation, so 'enduring' doesn't exist in Quebec.

questions.q: In a common-law province, for a power of attorney for property to stay in force during the grantor's mental incapacity, the document must expressly say so.
options: True
False
questions.explain: True. The enduring (continuing) nature must be spelled out in the document; otherwise the attorney's powers cease when the grantor becomes mentally incapable, just when they are needed most. Quebec uses a protection mandate instead.

questions.q: How can a protection mandate be made in Quebec?
options: Only by notarial act, with two of the mandator's relatives as witnesses
Only in the mandator's own handwriting, with no witnesses at all
By notarial act, or before two witnesses who have no interest in it
Before one witness, who must be the mandator's family doctor
questions.explain: A protection mandate is made by notarial act or in the presence of two witnesses with no interest in the deed, who certify that the mandator is of sound mind and capable. A witnessed mandate may be written by the mandator or by a third person.

questions.q: Manfred wants to give his son Hans a power of attorney over his finances, but worries Hans could use it to change his will. What should he be told?
options: Hans could change the will once a doctor declares Manfred to be incapable
Even an unrestricted power of attorney gives Hans no authority to change the will
Hans could change the will, but only if the power of attorney is expressly made enduring
Hans could change the will unless Manfred files a copy with his bank
questions.explain: An attorney can make almost any legal commitment the grantor could (buy and sell assets, borrow, sign contracts) but cannot make, change or revoke the grantor's will. Manfred could also limit Hans's authority to his bank and investment accounts with a restricted power of attorney.

questions.q: Lucie wants to name her two children as attorneys for property with the strongest protection against misuse. Which arrangement fits, and what is its drawback?
options: Joint: each may act alone, so one can step in whenever the other is away
Several: they check each other, but both must agree before either one can act
Several: they may act only after a court appoints a committee to oversee their decisions
Joint: they check each other, but both must be available and agree before acting
questions.explain: Joint attorneys must all concur, a check and balance against misuse, but all must be available and agree, risking deadlock and delay. Several (independent) authority is more flexible but gives up those checks. Corporate attorneys accept joint appointments but prefer not several.

questions.q: Which two conditions must be met before a protection mandate can be executed in Quebec?
options: The mandator is incapable, and the court has homologated the mandate
The mandator is incapable, and the Public Curator has signed the mandate
The mandatary accepts in writing, and the mandator's family consents
A doctor declares incapacity, and a notary registers the mandate
questions.explain: Under art. 2166 CCQ, performing the mandate depends on the mandator's incapacity and on homologation by the court at the mandatary's request; a medical and a psychosocial evaluation are mandatory. That is why the common-law 'enduring' concept doesn't exist in Quebec.

questions.q: What is a 'springing' (contingent) power of attorney?
options: One that passes automatically to a substitute attorney if the first resigns
One that a court activates by naming a committee once the grantor has become incapable
One that takes effect on signing and ends when the grantor becomes incapable
One that takes effect only when a person named in it declares the grantor incapable
questions.explain: Most powers of attorney take effect when signed, though normally used only on incapacity. A springing power grants authority only on a declaration of incapacity by an independent person named in it, such as the family doctor; third parties accept it once they receive that declaration.

questions.q: Sylvie, of Quebec, signs a document letting her brother sell her rental condo while she travels for four months, ending on her return date. What is this called in the Civil Code, and when would it lose validity?
options: A protection mandate, which must be homologated before her brother can act
An enduring power of attorney, which continues if she becomes incapable
A simple mandate, effective on signature, that ends if she becomes incapable
A dative tutorship, which the court must approve within 90 days of signing
questions.explain: In Quebec, a (simple) mandate, called a power of attorney in everyday language, lets a capable person be represented in absence. It is effective on signature and loses validity if the mandator loses capacity. Limiting it to one asset and a date is what common law calls a restricted power of attorney.

questions.q: In Quebec, a mandatary under a protection mandate may resign simply by notifying the mandator, just as under a simple mandate.
options: True
False
questions.explain: False. Under a protection mandate, the mandatary cannot resign without having found a substitute. Under a simple mandate (power of attorney), the mandatary need only advise the grantor of the resignation.

questions.q: In Quebec, to whom does a mandatary acting under a homologated protection mandate account, according to the course?
options: To the notary who drew up the mandate, through six-month reports
To the Public Curator, through annual accounts for as long as it lasts
To the mandator, who must approve each transaction in writing
To the heirs at the end of the administration, with no periodic reports
questions.explain: The mandatary accounts to the heirs at the end of the administration and is not subject to periodic accounting to the Public Curator, so it is wise to require accounting to a third party in the mandate. Elsewhere, an attorney becomes accountable to the court once the grantor is incapable.

questions.q: Which statement about a power of attorney for personal care in a common-law province is accurate?
options: It is valid only if the Canadian Medical Association has approved its wording
It can be used only once the grantor is mentally incapable, and never by a trust company
It takes effect on signing, and a trust company may hold it jointly with a relative
It covers investments as well as housing decisions, and it ends when the grantor becomes incapable
questions.explain: Unlike a property power of attorney, a personal care attorney cannot use the authority until the grantor is mentally incapable, since until then only the grantor decides on housing, food, clothing and treatment. A corporate attorney cannot be given (and would not accept) this role.

questions.q: How does a Quebec 'biological will' differ from a protection mandate?
options: It is a notarial deed that replaces the will and takes effect only at death
It names a mandatary for personal care and must be homologated before use
It covers only the person's property and leaves health decisions to the doctor
It just states treatment wishes and names no one to decide for the person
questions.explain: Unlike the formal protection mandate, the biological will is a simple document describing the grantor's wishes about treatment; it does not designate anyone to decide on his or her behalf. A protection mandate can cover both the person and property, even with different mandataries.

questions.q: Which advice about preparing an Advance Care Directive is consistent with the course?
options: Use broad wording such as 'no heroic measures' so the attorney has flexibility
Include instructions for euthanasia, which medical staff must then carry out
Leave out any attorney, since the directive itself makes every decision
Consult a doctor and give very specific instructions rather than vague phrases
questions.explain: A doctor should be consulted and instructions should be very specific; clear enough instructions must be followed by medical staff. Vague terms like 'no heroic measures' cause confusion, and instructions such as euthanasia are not likely to be followed under Canadian law.

questions.q: In Quebec, what can be done when a person becomes incapable without having made a protection mandate?
options: The person's will takes effect early, and the liquidator manages the property
The spouse automatically becomes the mandatary, with full powers over both property and the person
An interested person can ask the court to open a protective regime with a tutor or curator
A notary can homologate an unsigned draft mandate found among the person's papers
questions.explain: Any person who shows an interest can apply to court to open a protective regime, and a tutor or curator is appointed. Their authority resembles a mandatary's, but with less flexibility and power and without the person's own directions.

questions.q: According to the course, it is generally not in all parties' best interest for a financial planner to act as a client's attorney under a power of attorney.
options: True
False
questions.explain: True. The planner's role is to explain the advantages and risks of the different types of authority and structures, not to act as attorney. If a client seems increasingly confused, the planner should document the concerns and tell the family or lawyer.
